{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-House Legal
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement (Vendor form)
**Privileged & Confidential — Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our contracting playbook. Overall, the draft is unusually favourable to us: fifteen of the eighteen rules reviewed are compliant, and several sit at or above our preferred position (indemnification, assignment and change of control, termination for convenience, audit rights, renewal mechanics, transition assistance and insurance). Notably, the Agreement affirmatively disclaims exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-commitment and non-solicitation obligations on us, and the only MFN and competition restraints run in our favour.

Three items require negotiation:

- **§ 7.7 (Liquidated damages) — walk-away.** A late invoice triggers liquidated damages of fifteen percent of annual Fees *per week*. This fails our fallback and can compound past remaining contract value. We seek deletion.
- **§ 21 (Limitation of liability).** The cap is illusory because "Fees" is defined as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form. We seek a twelve-month fees cap; the carve-out set in § 21.3 is already strong and is preserved verbatim.
- **§ 14/15 (Customer Data licence scope).** Vendor's rights extend beyond providing the Services (improvement of the Services, and model training on consent). We seek to narrow to processing solely to provide the Services; ownership and the perpetual embedded-technology licence remain intact.

No other redlines are proposed. Minor shortfalls short of preferred wording (e.g. the ninety-day Deliverable conformance period and the "intentionally introduced" qualifier in § 19.3; the absence of a USD 1,000,000 liability floor; the competitor-assignment bar in § 24.2) are noted for information only.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables (with §§ 13.2, 15.1) | Customer Data licence extends beyond providing the Services (improvement; model training on consent). Ownership and assignment provisions are compliant. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification | Meets preferred position in full; uncapped via § 21.3 Excluded Claims, better than the 3× annual fees fallback. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) | 15% of annual Fees per week for late invoice; fails fallback and sits in walk-away territory. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control | Substantially at preferred position; Customer may assign to Affiliate/successor without consent; no Vendor change-of-control termination right. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities (§ 12.3) | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; § 12.4 restraint runs against Vendor. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence | Preferred position met; revocation narrower than our standard (§ 13.3). |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities (§ 12.3) | Express confirmation of no non-compete or field/territory restraint. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination (§ 9.4; § 29.4) | Unconditional Customer right, 30 days' notice, pro rata refund, no early-termination fee; Vendor has no convenience right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights | Every preferred element met; no direct system access; findings are our Confidential Information. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution | New York law; exclusive New York County jurisdiction; no arbitration. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.6) | Only MFN runs in our favour; no obligation on us to match or disclose third-party terms. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope (§ 2.1) | No minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall penalty; at preferred position. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities (§ 12.3) | No no-hire covenant; general recruitment expressly preserved. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal (§§ 8.2–8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30 days' opt-out, 60-day reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return | Six months' assistance, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion; assistance priced at expiring Order Form rates. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant (fallback) | § 19 Warranties | Sits at the fallback on material terms; disclaimer in § 19.5 does not swallow express warranties. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance | All preferred limits met, including USD 5m cyber and privacy; certificates on request. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability | Cap tied to the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form; fails the 12-month fees fallback. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

1. **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** Fifteen percent of annual Fees per week for a late invoice is the only liquidated-damages mechanic in the document and it runs entirely against us. It is not an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees, so it fails our fallback, and a minor payment delay can compound past the remaining contract value. Our position: delete the charge and confirm unconditionally that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by us. No other clause depends on § 7.7 (§ 7.3 merely restricts Vendor from charging interest on amounts not due), so deletion is clean.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. **Issue redlines on the three deviations only** — § 7.7 (delete Customer-payable liquidated damages), § 21.1 (cap restated as fees paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event, retaining every § 21.3 carve-out verbatim), and §§ 14.1/15.1 (narrow Vendor's Customer Data licence to processing solely to provide the Services).
2. **Confirm the § 21 drafting mechanics with the deal team.** The words "and all Order Forms" are required to displace the retained "first Order Form" restriction, and lowercase "fees" is used in its ordinary sense so that the defined term "Fees" (§ 1.5) continues to operate unchanged in § 21.3 and elsewhere.
3. **Escalate § 7.7 internally before the next negotiation call** so that the walk-away characterisation is agreed at the business level and we do not trade it against a lower-value point.
4. **Do not reopen compliant clauses.** Several provisions exceed our preferred position (uncapped Vendor indemnity, six-month transition assistance, § 22 audit protections, § 24.4 change-of-control protection, Vendor-granted MFN in § 7.6, Vendor-side restraint in § 12.4). We should hold these as drafted.
5. **Record the noted-only items** in the deal file for renewal diligence: the ninety-day Deliverable conformance period and the "intentionally introduced" malicious-code qualifier (§ 19), the absence of a USD 1,000,000 liability floor and the "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" payment carve-out (§ 21.3), the consent-based rather than absolute competitor-assignment bar (§ 24.2), and the 30-day data-return clock running from our request (§ 11.2) — a timing point we control."}
